To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of a functioning spleen in a recipient can facilitate the acceptance, or at least prolong the life of, a kidney allograft, depending on the donor and recipient strain combination.
the presence of a donor spleen facilitates the acceptance of a simultaneously implanted kidney graft to various extents, depending on the donor-recipient strain combination.
vascularized spleens can facilitate kidney graft acceptance, but the effect is strain specific.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the spleen as an accessory immune organ.
the immunological properties of the spleen and their potential use in transplantation.
the development of an immunosuppressive protocol for kidney transplantation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a vascularized spleen can facilitate graft acceptance in the absence of host splenectomy.
the spleen grafts are capable of facilitating the acceptance of simultaneous kidney grafts, but that this is not a universal phenomenon.
the donor spleen is a powerful immunomodulating agent, capable of facilitating the acceptance of vascularized organ grafts in the absence of any other form of immunosuppression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the donor spleen facilitates the acceptance of the simultaneous heart, liver, kidney, or lung graft, and that the effect can be unidirectional or bidirectional.
the spleen can facilitate acceptance of simultaneously implanted vascularized grafts in a variety of combinations, provided that host splenectomy follows the graft implantation.
the spleen is a potent facilitator for the induction of tolerance, but the degree of facilitation depends on the strain combination and the nature of the graft.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spleen grafts may be useful to improve the outcome of simultaneous renal transplantation in humans.
the spleen is not only a potent source for the production of alloreactive antibodies, but also a major contributor of the alloreactive T cell response.
the spleen is a major player in the immune response to vascularized solid organ transplants.
